h1: Analytics that agrees with your bank statement
metaTitle: GA4 Analytics Setup Services — Fixed ₹75,000 Build
metaDescription: GA4 analytics setup services that end in a signed measurement plan. Every form, WhatsApp click and UPI payment tracked properly, for a fixed ₹75,000 build.
answer: A GA4 analytics setup project defines every event your business cares about, builds and QAs the tracking, then reconciles what GA4 reports against what your payment gateway actually paid you. Ours ends with a signed measurement plan and a reconciliation sheet. Fixed fee of ₹75,000, one-time, GST extra.
takeaways: The deliverable is a **signed measurement plan** — event names, triggers, parameters, owners and definitions — agreed before a single tag is built.
We reconcile GA4 purchase counts against your Razorpay or Shopify payout data before handover. If they don't agree within 5%, it isn't finished.
WhatsApp clicks, call taps and UPI payments are the three things Indian sites track worst. All three need specific handling, not a default tag.
GA4's default data retention is two months. Almost nobody changes it. If yours is still on the default, you've already lost data you can't get back.
No performance guarantee attaches to this build, and we'll explain why rather than pretend otherwise.

sections.h2: The measurement plan is the deliverable, not the tag
body: Most analytics projects begin with someone installing GA4 and end with an argument in month three about whether a WhatsApp click counts as a lead. The argument is the real problem, and it's a documentation problem, not a technical one.
So we start with a spreadsheet and don't touch the tag manager until you've signed it. It is unglamorous and it is the entire value of the engagement.

callout.title: Sign it before the build
callout.body: Getting your sales lead and your marketing lead to agree in writing on what a qualified lead is takes about forty minutes and saves a quarter. If they can't agree, that's the finding — and it's worth more than the tracking.

body: Once the plan is signed, the build is mechanical. These are the parts that get missed most often, in our experience of opening other people's containers.
bullets: **GA4 property configuration** — data retention moved off the two-month default to 14 months, internal traffic filtered by IP, cross-domain linking, unwanted referrals excluded so your payment gateway doesn't get credit for every sale.
**Google Tag Manager container** — one container, documented, with a naming convention and no orphan tags left behind by the last agency.
**Key events** — the ones from the plan, marked as key events in GA4 and imported into Google Ads where they belong.
**Consent handling** — Consent Mode where you have EU traffic or a cookie banner. If you serve only India, we'll tell you plainly that you probably don't need the complexity yet.
**Search Console and Ads links**, plus a Looker Studio view that shows the six numbers you actually check, not the 40 GA4 offers.

**Server-side tagging, only when it pays for itself.** It adds a hosting bill and a maintenance surface. Our rule: below roughly ₹5 lakh a month in ad spend, or without meaningful iOS traffic, it costs more than it recovers. We'll say no.

sections.h2: The three conversions Indian sites get wrong
body: Default GA4 tracking was designed for a card-first, single-page checkout in a desktop browser. Indian funnels leave that model constantly, and the tracking silently under-reports every time they do.

A wa.me link unloads your page and opens an app. A click event fired on navigation frequently never reaches Google's servers, and in-app browsers make it worse. We fire on pointer-down with a beacon transport, and we append a prefilled message carrying the page reference so your sales team can see which page produced which chat.
What we can't do is follow the conversation. Unless you run the WhatsApp Business API, attribution ends at the click, and any agency claiming otherwise is guessing.

A tel: link tap is trackable. A person reading the number off your header and dialling it from their phone is not. If phone calls are your main channel, the honest answer is a call-tracking number, not a cleverer tag.

This is the big one. A UPI intent payment throws the user into GPay or PhonePe, and a large share never come back to your thank-you page. If your purchase event lives on that page, you are under-counting revenue — sometimes badly enough that paid campaigns look unprofitable when they aren't.

The fix is to fire the purchase server-side from the gateway webhook using the Measurement Protocol, with the transaction ID as the deduplication key against the client-side event. It's a day of work and it's usually the single most valuable thing in the whole build.

sections.h2: Reconciliation: the step that ends the arguments
body: This is what separates a tracking build from a tracking build that's finished. Before handover we pull a fixed window — usually the last full month — and put three columns side by side: GA4 purchases, gateway settlements, and orders in your backend.
They will not match perfectly. They never do, and any agency that shows you an exact match has either got lucky or filtered the sheet. What matters is that every gap has a name.
bullets: **Refunds and cancellations** counted as purchases in one system and not the other.
**COD orders** that were placed but never paid, or paid weeks later.
**Consent declines and ad blockers**, which remove sessions from GA4 entirely and can never be recovered client-side.
**Cross-device journeys**, where the research happened on mobile and the payment on a laptop.
**Failed and retried payments** that create two attempts and one settlement.

callout.title: Our acceptance criterion
callout.body: Purchase counts within 5% of gateway settlements for the reconciliation window, with every remaining gap named in the sheet. If it's outside that, the build isn't done and we don't invoice the final milestone. A 30% gap — which is what we usually find on arrival — means every decision made off that data last year was made blind.

sections.h2: Price, timeline, and why there's no guarantee on this one
body: **₹75,000, fixed, one-time.** GST extra. Two to four weeks, depending on how many payment paths you have and how quickly your developers can give us access. Multi-country properties, a headless storefront, or a gateway with no webhook support push it to the upper end, and we'll tell you before you pay, not during.

Everything is yours: the GTM container, the measurement plan, the dashboards, the documentation. There is nothing in a Last Agency analytics build that another agency couldn't pick up on day one, which is deliberate.

Now the awkward bit. Our 90-day guarantee — beat your frozen baseline of qualified organic leads or we keep working free — does not apply to this project, and we won't pretend it does. A tracking build doesn't create demand. It tells you the truth about the demand you already have, and sometimes that truth is worse than the fiction you were reporting. Attaching a performance promise to measurement work would be selling you a coin toss with our name on it.
What it does do is make the guarantee possible everywhere else. You cannot freeze a baseline you can't measure, which is why most [SEO engagements](/seo) that start with us start here.

faqs.q: How much does GA4 setup cost in India?
faqs.a: Agency builds range from about ₹25,000 for a basic tag install to ₹2,00,000+ for multi-property, server-side setups with CRM integration. Ours is a fixed ₹75,000 ex-GST for a single property including the measurement plan, server-side purchase confirmation and reconciliation against your payment data.

faqs.q: How long does an analytics setup project take?
faqs.a: Two to four weeks. Roughly a week on the audit and measurement plan, a week on the build, and a week on QA and reconciliation. The variable is almost never our side — it's how fast we get access to the tag manager, the gateway and a developer who can add one script.

Only if you have real ad spend, meaningful iOS traffic, or payments that complete off your site. Server-side tagging adds a monthly hosting bill and something else that can break. Our threshold is roughly ₹5 lakh a month in ad spend — below that, a well-built client-side setup with webhook-confirmed purchases does the job.

faqs.q: Why doesn't GA4 match my Razorpay or Shopify numbers?
faqs.a: Usually because UPI payments complete inside a banking app and the user never returns to your thank-you page, so the client-side purchase event never fires. Add refunds, ad blockers, consent declines and cross-device sessions and a 20–30% gap is common. Firing the purchase from the gateway webhook closes most of it.

faqs.q: Can you fix an existing GA4 setup instead of rebuilding it?
faqs.a: Often, yes, and it's cheaper. We audit first and tell you honestly whether the container is salvageable. Sometimes it isn't — years of orphan tags from three agencies with no naming convention takes longer to untangle than to replace, and we'll say so with the reasons.

faqs.q: Who owns the analytics setup if we stop working with you?
faqs.a: You do, entirely. The GA4 property, the GTM container, the measurement plan, the dashboards and the documentation are yours from day one and stay yours. We don't host anything on our own accounts, and we don't need a call before releasing access.
